# dsh-window-control
**English** · 简体中文

Give an LLM agent **eyes and hands on an already-running Windows desktop**: enumerate
and find windo

ws, screenshot windows that are completely covered by others, read UI
through OCR / template matchin

g / UI Automation, click and type for real, and drive
Chrome over the DevTools Protocol.

It ships as a Python package (`winctl`) plus a **DeepSeek Harness** plugin that registers
it as an M

CP server, so the model gets **37 native tools** named `mcp__window__*`.
Everything is also usable f
rom the CLI or as a plain Python library.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why

Most "computer use" stacks need a browser, a VM or a screenshot-only loop. The common
real-world cas

e is a **live desktop with apps someone else is using**: an Electron/CEF
streaming tool, WeChat, a U

WP settings page, a browser with 40 tabs. `winctl` handles
exactly that:

- **Nothing to instrument.** No accessibility tree? Fall back to pixels. No pixels
because the windo

w is covered? Capture it directly with `PrintWindow`/DWM.
- **Honest results.** Every call returns `

{"ok", "data", "error", "elapsed_ms"}`.
A click that could not be delivered says `sendinput_unavaila

ble: uipi_blocked …`
instead of pretending it worked; a `set_value` is read back and verified.
- **N

on-invasive by default.** Background actions optionally restore the previous
foreground window; `wor

k_area`-aware window placement; the browser layer always uses
its **own** Chrome profile and port in
stead of hijacking yours.
## Features
| Layer | What you get |
| **Windows** | Enumerate/inspect/activate/move/close windows, `WindowFromPoint`, client↔screen mapp
ing, PerMonitorV2 DPI — all coordinates are physical pixels, multi-monitor and negative virtual orig

ins included |
| **Capture** | `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` → DWM → BitBlt → screen-region fa
llback chain; captures fully occluded windows, never masks or fakes content; only failure case is a

minimized window |
| **UI Automation** | Flattened tree dump with `index`/`depth`/`parent_index`/`pa
tterns`, find by name/regex/type/automation-id, actions (`invoke/set_value/toggle/select/expand/coll

apse/scroll_into_view/send_keys`) with **read-back verification** |
| **Vision** | RapidOCR (`rapido
cr-onnxruntime`, Chinese+English) with a WinRT OCR fallback, multi-scale template matching (`cv2.mat

chTemplate` + NMS), diff ratio, dark-UI preprocessing |
| **Input** | Absolute-coordinate `SendInput
`, `PostMessage` background clicks/typing (Unicode, emoji), hotkeys, drag/scroll, `restore_foregroun

d` |
| **Browser** | Chrome DevTools Protocol over `websocket-client` (no Playwright/Selenium): laun

ch own instance, tabs, `Runtime.evaluate`, DOM query/click/type/wait, tab screenshots |
| **Orchestr
ation** | One locator DSL (`kind = uia / image / ocr / coords`, `auto` = automatic degradation) and
`win_sequence` for multi-step flows |
## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (x64), **Python 3.11+**
- Dependencies: `python -m pip install -r requirements.tx

t`
- Optional: DeepSeek Harness for the plugin route (the CLI/library route needs no DSH)
- Chrome/E
dge for the CDP layer (edge is auto-detected), and the optional OCR extra
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Install as a DSH plugin

The plugin folder `dsh-plugin/` is a config-only DSH bundle named
`dsh-window-control`; it registers

the server under `serverName: window`. There are two
routes — **route 1 also lists the plugin in DS
H's plugin directory/panel**.
### Route 1 — install as a plugin bundle (recommended)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script does what the DSH plugin manager does for a local plugin: copies the bundle
to `%USERPROF

ILE%\.dsh\plugins\dsh-window-control`, fills in your real `python.exe` and
repository paths, adds th

e dependency plus `dsh.profile.bundles` entry to the profile
`package.json`, links it into `node_mod

ules` (a junction, so no `pnpm install`), and
removes the legacy patch entry so the MCP server is no

t registered twice. Afterwards the
plugin is listed in the plugin panel and the model has 37 `mcp__w

ce. Afterwards the
plugin is listed in the plugin panel and the model has 37 `mcp__window__*` tools.

Useful flags: `-Python C:\Python311\python.exe` (python not on `PATH`), `-Profile <name>`,

`-Uninstall`.

## Limitations (read before complaining 🙂)

- **UIPI / elevated foreground.** If an **administrator-elevated window owns the
foreground**, Windo

ws blocks `SetCursorPos`/`SendInput`/`PostMessage` from a
non-elevated process. `winctl` detects thi

s and returns
`sendinput_unavailable: uipi_blocked …`. Fix: focus a normal window, or run DSH/the
ca

ller **as administrator**. (`win_input_state` diagnoses it in one call.)
- **CEF / Qt shells expose

no UIA content.** `uia_usable: false` is not a bug — use the
vision layer. Detection short-circuits

in ≤16 ms, so it never hangs.
- **Chrome 136+** refuses `--remote-debugging-port` on the default pro

file, so the CDP
layer always launches **its own** instance (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\winctl-chrome-profile`,

port 9333). It will not attach to your everyday Chrome profile.
- **`win_click` restores the previo

us foreground by default**, so “click then type”
needs an explicit `win_window_activate` in between

(or a type call targeting the
window directly).
- **`verified` semantics.** `invoke/click` cannot be

read back — they report
`verified: false` meaning “dispatched”, not “UI changed”. `set_value/type/t

oggle/
select` are read back and fail loudly with `type_verify_failed`.
- **`mode="message"`** never

steals focus, but CEF/Chromium apps often ignore posted
`WM_*` messages (`effective: null`).
- Wind

ows that require elevation themselves (Task Manager, UAC prompts) cannot be
automated from a normal-

integrity process.
